episodes.title: Sharing the road with driverless cars
episodes.description: Imagine crossing a road and turning to see a car heading towards you... without a driver! While this might seem scary, driverless cars are already operating safely in many cities around the world. These autonomous cars contain huge amounts of technology to help them drive alongside other road users carefully. But will humans behave as carefully around them? Can we communicate clearly with these 'robotaxis', or are we simply incompatible? Phil and Pippa discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. Learn English from authentic BBC programme clips. episodes.title: Who does the housework?
episodes.description: Unloading the dishwasher, mopping the floor, cleaning the loo... what is your most hated household chore? We all know there are jobs around the house which have to be done regularly, even if they are sometimes boring or unpleasant. But who tends to do the most amount of jobs in your household? And is there anyone who isn't pulling their weight...? Pippa and Neil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. Learn English from authentic BBC programme clips. episodes.title: How do climate scientists make predictions?
episodes.description: Across the world, climate change is already beginning to change the way we live our lives. But how big will that change be and what kinds of change will occur? These are the kinds of questions that scientists have been asking for decades. So, how exactly do they try to find answers to such complex questions about the future? Understanding where we are heading might help humanity prepare for the consequences of climate change. Phil and Pippa discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. Learn English from authentic BBC programme clips. Get a free worksheet, quiz...
episodes.titleZh: 气候科学家如何做出预测？

episodes.descZh: 1788年，国王乔治三世开始不停地讲话，与树木交谈，恐吓他的宫廷。他经常被人们铭记为失去美国的“疯王”，但他的生活要复杂得多和悲惨得多。这一集讲述了这位忠诚的农民国王、他的神秘疾病，以及医生现在认为他确实出了问题。乔治三世超越了疯狂国王的刻板印象早年生活和成为英国人而不是德国国王农民乔治的习惯和对家庭和科学的热爱七年战争的胜利和英国的沉重债务导致了美国革命和独立.

episodes.title: #622 | A Short History of Fire
episodes.description: A million years ago, in a cave in South Africa, our ancestors did something no other animal has ever done: they controlled fire. Fire cooked our food, shrank our guts, grew our brains, and gave us the deep sleep and fireside stories that made us human. This is the story of our species' oldest technology, and how the same flames that built the modern world may now threaten it. episodes.titleZh: #622|火的简史
episodes.descZh: 一百万年前，在南非的一个洞穴里，我们的祖先做了一件其他动物从未做过的事情：他们控制火。火煮了我们的食物，收缩了我们的内脏，生长了我们的大脑，给了我们沉睡的睡眠和炉边故事，这些故事让我们成为人类。这是我们物种最古老技术的故事，以及建造现代世界的火焰现在如何威胁它。Wonderwerk洞穴证据表明直立人控制火早期人类为了温暖、光明和安全而管理火烹饪增加.

The reason is French Guiana, a territory on the northeastern coast of South America which is officially part of France. French Guiana isn't the only surprising part of France. France has territories and departments in the Caribbean, the Indian Ocean, the Pacific...

But do proficiency tests actually help you in your goal to become fluent in English? episodes.titleZh: 英语考试：它们能改善教育吗？（英语词汇课）
episodes.descZh: 英语考试无处不在。听这一集的许多人已经花了（或目前正在花）数月的时间准备IETS、TOEFL、TOEIC和剑桥英语资格等考试。如果您想出国留学、获得新工作资格或搬到另一个国家，通常需要通过能力测试。但能力测试真的能帮助您实现流利英语的目标吗？对于某些人来说，英语考试为激励您的学习提供了明确的目标，并提供了衡量语言能力的公平方法。其他人则认为测试鼓励.

It is known for its colourful carnival celebrations, the Christ the Redeemer statue and white beaches, and of course its association with football and samba music. Its history is also fascinating! Today I want to discuss how the city got its names, became the centre of battles...

episodes.title: It's Greek to me: Why is the language of 'The Odyssey' shorthand for all that we don’t understand?
episodes.description: 1214. This week, we look at why we say, "It's all Greek to me" when we don't understand something. We trace the phrase from medieval monks who couldn't read Greek manuscripts to Shakespeare's "Julius Caesar," and look at how other languages, like Czech, German, and Cantonese, express the same idea of incomprehension. The Greek segment was written by Valerie Fridland, a professor of linguistics at the University of Nevada in Reno and author of "Why We Talk Funny: The Real Story Behind Our Accents." You can find her at valeriefridland.com. A hearty thank-you...

In epidemiology, this central character is known as Patient Zero—the case at the heart of an outbreak. This hour, Radiolab digs up an episode we first produced in 2011 and hunts for Patient Zeroes from all over the map. We start with the story of perhaps the most iconic Patient Zero of all time: Typhoid Mary. Then, we dive into a molecular detective story to pinpoint the beginning of the AIDS, and we re-imagine the...
